name: LSM6DSO32 accelerometer & gyroscope
description: STMicroelectronics 6-axis IMU: 3-axis accelerometer with an extended ±4/8/16/32 g range and 3-axis gyroscope (±125–2000 dps) plus a die temperature sensor, read over I2C (or SPI). The chip runs on 1.71–3.6 V; the breakout adds a 3.3 V regulator and level shifting so it takes 3–5 V. Sold as: Adafruit LSM6DSO32 6-DoF Accelerometer and Gyroscope - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (#4692), main 9-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA, DO, CS, I1, I2 (5-pin auxiliary SCX, SDX, CS, DO, GND header not modelled), STEMMA QT connectors, I2C address 0x6A (0x6B with DO high or the AD0 jumper bridged), 10 kΩ I2C pull-ups fitted; may ship with the pin-compatible LSM6DSO32X.
eli5: Feels which way it is tilted, how hard it is shaken (up to 32 times gravity) and how fast it is spinning.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply 3–5 V into the on-board 3.3 V regulator (use the same voltage as your board's logic)

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (SPI SCK); level shifted, 10 kΩ pull-up on the board

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (SPI SDI); level shifted, 10 kΩ pull-up on the board

pins.name: DO
pins.description: I2C address bit SDO/SA0: low or unconnected = 0x6A, high = 0x6B (SPI data out); leave unconnected for I2C

pins.name: CS
pins.description: Mode select: leave unconnected (pulled up = I2C mode); SPI chip select

pins.name: I1
pins.description: INT1 interrupt output (e.g. data ready), not needed for basic use

pins.name: I2
pins.description: INT2 interrupt output, not needed for basic use

buildNotes: Power VIN with 3.3 V or 5 V (the board regulates to 3.3 V and level-shifts SCL/SDA); never feed 3Vo.
Leave CS unconnected so the chip stays in I2C mode, and leave DO unconnected for address 0x6A (pull DO high or bridge AD0 for 0x6B).

Check WHO_AM_I (register 0x0F) reads 0x6C first; then write CTRL3_C = 0x44 (BDU + auto-increment), CTRL1_XL = 0x40 (104 Hz, ±4 g) and CTRL2_G = 0x40 (104 Hz, ±250 dps). Both sensors are powered down until you do.
Outputs are 16-bit two's complement, low byte first: accel 0x28–0x2D (0.122 mg/LSB at ±4 g), gyro 0x22–0x27 (8.75 mdps/LSB at ±250 dps), temperature 0x20–0x21 (25 °C + raw/256).
Accelerometer full-scale codes differ from the LSM6DSOX: FS_XL 00 = ±4 g, 01 = ±32 g, 10 = ±8 g, 11 = ±16 g. There is no ±2 g range, so LSM6DSOX code reads half the true acceleration.
The temperature output is the die temperature, not an air thermometer.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from lsm6dso32 import LSM6DSO32

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
imu = LSM6DSO32(i2c)  # 0x6A: Adafruit default (DO low)
while True:
    ax, ay, az = imu.acceleration()
    gx, gy, gz = imu.gyro()
    t = imu.temperature()
    print('A=%.2f,%.2f,%.2fg G=%.1f,%.1f,%.1fdps T=%.1fC' % (ax, ay, az, gx, gy, gz, t))
    time.sleep(1)
